questions.history: Decode a single buffer containing a\rXY\nb
questions.prediction: The PR reports first string a\rX on the parent. The merge should emit [a\rXY, b] and complete.
questions.basis: The LF ends the first line. X and Y separate it from the earlier CR, so no CRLF occurs there.
questions.refutation: The first merged string loses Y, the CR disappears, or the unterminated tail b is lost.

questions.history: Decode a\r\nb and a\nb in separate subscriptions
questions.prediction: Both revisions should yield [a, b] in each case.
questions.basis: Contiguous CRLF and a single LF are both configured separators. No payload bytes lie between the two bytes of the CRLF.
questions.refutation: A delimiter byte remains in the decoded string, a character disappears, or an extra line appears.

questions.history: Keep the UTF-8 bytes of é\r\r\nZ fixed. Compare a single buffer with buffers split at every byte, including within é
questions.prediction: The merge should produce the same two strings [é\r, Z] for both segmentations.
questions.basis: Only the second CR and following LF are adjacent. Neither the first CR nor either UTF-8 byte of é belongs to the delimiter.
questions.refutation: Segmentation changes a string, an encoding replacement appears, or both carriage returns are stripped.
